vocab.source: Source: Samuel Barrios technical learning list, October 13, 2026.

sections.root: Root breakdown: Latin componere "to put together, to collect a whole from several parts" = com ("with, together") + ponere ("to place"). Literally "something placed together with others" to make a whole.
sections.entered: Entered English from Latin componentem (nominative componens), present participle of componere.
sections.use1560s: First recorded use 1560s: "one of a group of persons."
sections.adjective1660s: 1660s: adjective "constituent, entering into the composition of."
sections.mechanical1896: 1896: "mechanical part of a bicycle, automobile, etc."
sections.today: Today: the same idea of a reusable building block is what React components are.

sections.what: What MCP is: an open protocol (started by Anthropic) where MCP servers expose tools, resources and prompts to MCP clients such as Cursor, Claude Code and Grok Bot. It's what turns a chat model into an agent that can act.
sections.kinds: Tools / resources / prompts: tools are actions, resources are read-only data and prompts are reusable templates. Knowing which is which lets you design safe, read-only connectors the way Policy 01 requires.
sections.transports: Transports (stdio, Streamable HTTP/SSE): this decides whether a server runs on your machine or on sam-erp-cloud-1.
sections.functionCalling: How it relates to function calling: each MCP tool is a JSON-Schema-described function. The client turns MCP tools into the model's function-calling list.
sections.orchestration: How it relates to orchestration: ED and its workers become far more capable when they share the same MCP servers instead of custom glue code.
sections.auth: Auth and scopes (OAuth, tokens, least privilege): connectors act as you, so their scope should be the smallest that works.
sections.already: You already use it: GitHub, Google Drive, Calendar, Stitch, Finance and X connectors are MCP namespaces. Your repo's only MCP mention is in tests/test_ai_core_cli.py.
sections.next: Next steps: 1. Read the MCP spec quickstart and run the official Python SDK (FastMCP) "hello" server. 2. Build a read-only Sam ERP MCP server on top of BOT-API with tools like list_clients, get_ticket and due_dates. 3. Add it to Cursor's mcp.json so Cursor cloud agents can query ERP data. 4. Write it as a ticket for the Claude lane with the usual scope rules. 5. Add tests with MCP Inspector.

sections.anthropic: Anthropic: the AI company that makes Claude. Your Claude lane runs Claude Code, so Anthropic's limits, models and docs shape one of your two coding workers.
sections.dispatcher: Dispatcher/worker pattern: this is exactly ED → Claude lane / Cursor, so learning it helps you tune your routing.
sections.queues: Load balancing and queues: your 2-ticket rule is a basic scheduler, and queue theory will help you improve it.
sections.routing: Model routing and model pinning: you pick models by cost, quota and skill. The Antigravity quota burnout shows why this matters.
sections.hitl: Human-in-the-loop approvals: these are central to Policy 01.
sections.handoffs: Handoffs and result contracts: .result.md outbox files are a handoff protocol, and formalizing them reduces errors.
sections.subagents: Subagents and context windows: splitting work keeps each agent focused and cheap.
sections.limits: Rate limits and quotas: these explain stalls and failed runs.

sections.system: System prompts and standing instructions: your hub is in effect a shared system prompt.
sections.spec: Spec-style prompts (scope, constraints, acceptance criteria): your CURSOR tickets already do this, so make it a template.
sections.fewShot: Few-shot examples: these raise output consistency for tax and bookkeeping formats.
sections.structured: Structured output (JSON mode): lets bots return data your ERP can parse.
sections.injection: Prompt injection: emails and web pages can hide instructions, which is a real risk for Claims Hunter and Fix Inbox.
sections.versioning: Prompt versioning: keeps changes to the hub auditable.

sections.calling: Function calling: how models call your code, and the base layer under MCP.
sections.schemas: Tool schemas (JSON Schema): clear parameter schemas mean fewer bad tool calls.
sections.idempotency: Idempotency: a retried tool call shouldn't run twice, for example a duplicate payment.
sections.dryRun: Dry run / read-only mode: matches your "read-only toward the outside world" rule.

sections.rag: RAG: feeds agents your real documents (policies, client PDFs) instead of guesses.
sections.chunking: Chunking: how you split PDFs from PDF Studio affects answer quality.
sections.rerank: Reranking and hybrid search: keyword plus meaning is best for tax forms and IDs.
sections.citations: Citations and grounding: tax answers must point to their source.

sections.embeddings: Embeddings: text turned into vectors so you can search by meaning, for example "find similar expense descriptions".
sections.cosine: Cosine similarity: the core math behind semantic search.
sections.models: Embedding models and dimensions: these set the cost/quality trade-off.

sections.options: pgvector / SQLite-vec / Chroma / Qdrant: where embeddings live. pgvector fits a FastAPI + Postgres ERP.
sections.metadata: Metadata filtering: keeps client A's documents out of client B's answers, which matters for privacy.
sections.hnsw: Indexes (HNSW): keep searches fast as data grows.

sections.rest: REST, HTTP methods, status codes (303, 401, 429): you already verified these in hardening.
sections.openapi: OpenAPI / FastAPI docs: FastAPI writes API schemas automatically, and agents can read them.
sections.oauth: OAuth 2.0 and service accounts: used by your Google Forms import and Drive backups.
sections.webhooks: Webhooks: event-driven syncs for the Financial Hub.
sections.jsonrpc: JSON-RPC: used by odoo_rpc.py and also by MCP itself.
sections.pagination: Pagination, retries and backoff: needed for reliable syncs.

sections.scraping: Scraping (requests, BeautifulSoup): the MGE scraper and the gold-elite raw pages.
sections.cron: Cron / schedulers: the MGE VM, Always-Running and due-date reminders.
sections.robots: robots.txt and ToS: keep scraping legal.

sections.playwright: Playwright: your screenshot QA and QC E2E tool.
sections.selectors: Selectors and locators: the reason stable tests pass.
sections.headless: Headless browsers, visual regression and screenshot diffing: catch design breaks automatically.
sections.profiles: Browser profiles and cookies: know what a logged-in profile can access.

sections.diffs: Diffs and patches: how you review what agents changed.
sections.allowlists: File-scope allowlists: your ticket "Scope (files allowed)" rule.
sections.pdf: PDF parsing and OCR (pdfplumber, PyMuPDF, Tesseract): the core of tax document intake.
sections.linters: Linters/formatters (ESLint, Stylelint, ruff): keep agent code consistent.

evaluation.title: Evaluation and testing of AI systems

sections.unit: Unit/integration tests (pytest, Vitest): the pass/fail gate ED uses.
sections.e2e: E2E tests: the QC E2E suite.
sections.evals: Evals and golden datasets: measure whether the Claims optimizer or Bookkeeper is actually improving.
sections.selfCheck: Self-check / self-critique loops: the Bookkeeper self-check, and they need ground truth.
sections.regression: Regression, flaky tests and test fixtures: synthetic fixtures protect client data.
sections.judge: LLM-as-judge: automated grading, with known biases.

sections.least: Least privilege and scoped tokens: limit what each bot can do.
sections.secrets: Secrets management (.env, never commit secrets): your tickets already forbid touching these.
sections.csrf: CSRF, rate limiting, security headers, default deny: your PR55–59 work.
sections.breakGlass: Break-glass access: your emergency path from PR58.
sections.ssrf: SSRF / URL guards: your url-guard tests.
sections.injection: Prompt injection and data exfiltration: the main new risk with agent tools.
sections.audit: Audit logs: prove who did what.
sections.tailscale: Tailscale and Funnel: private network vs public exposure. You verified Funnel is off.

sections.loop: Branch → commit → push → PR → review → merge: the loop every ticket follows.
sections.rebase: Rebase vs merge, merge conflicts: you'll hit these when parallel agents edit the same files.
sections.protected: Protected branches / rulesets: enforce "never push main" technically, not only by policy.
sections.actions: GitHub Actions, workflows, secrets: your Claude lane runs on these.
sections.worktrees: Git worktrees: your wt-task-* folders, so agents can work in parallel without clobbering each other.
sections.pages: GitHub Pages: static hosting for sites.
sections.semver: Semantic versioning (VERSION) and tags/releases: track what's deployed.

sections.python: Python: the main language of Sam ERP (~5,900 .py files including deps) and division-one-bots (224 .py).
sections.ts: TypeScript: JavaScript with types, used in sam-erp/frontend. It catches bugs before runtime.
sections.html: HTML / Jinja2 templates: page structure. Jinja fills HTML on the server.
sections.shell: Shell (bash): deploy and ops scripts (16 .sh in division-one-bots).
sections.yaml: YAML: config for Actions and tickets.
sections.markdown: Markdown: docs, tickets and the hub.
sections.gas: Google Apps Script: JavaScript for Google Workspace (Forms).
sections.sql: SQL: the language of your database, to learn alongside the ORM.

sections.react: React: a UI library built from components. Sam ERP's frontend uses React + react-router-dom, and you told me samuel-learn uses React + Vite.
sections.hooks: Components, props, state, hooks (useState, useEffect): the core React ideas agents write every day.
sections.vite: Vite: a fast dev server and bundler (dev server, HMR, vite build → dist/). It's used in sam-erp/frontend and takeod-site.
sections.vitest: Vitest: Vite's test runner, already in your frontend.
sections.css: CSS basics: styles are rules made of a selector (which elements), properties (what to change) and values (how). Classes are reusable selectors.
sections.box: Box model: content + padding + border + margin, the cause of most spacing bugs.
sections.media: Media queries: responsive design for phone and iPad.
sections.vars: Custom properties (--var): CSS variables. This is how design tokens and themes like DRAGON/SCORPIO work.
sections.cascade: Cascade and specificity: why one rule beats another.
sections.cssReact: CSS in React: className instead of class, CSS Modules (scoped per component), Tailwind utility classes (which you already use), and inline styles for dynamic values.
sections.tokens: Design tokens and design systems: keep Stitch mockups and code consistent.
sections.a11y: Accessibility (semantic HTML, contrast, focus): usable by everyone, and better for SEO.

sections.schema: Database schema: tables, columns, types and keys. It's the shape of ERP data.
sections.orm: ORM (SQLAlchemy etc.): Python objects mapped to tables.
sections.jsonSchema: JSON Schema: describes valid JSON, used for configs and tool definitions.
sections.openapi: API schemas (OpenAPI): a contract between front end, back end and bots (BOT-API).
sections.toolSchemas: Tool schemas: JSON Schema for function calling and MCP tools.
sections.clientServer: Frontend / backend, client-server: the browser talks to FastAPI on sam-erp-cloud-1.
sections.monolith: Monolith vs microservices: Sam ERP is a modular monolith (app/modules/*), which is right at your size.
sections.mvc: MVC / layered architecture, API layer, data model: where code belongs.
sections.soc: Separation of concerns: small, focused modules make agent tickets safer to scope.
sections.factory: App factory and dependency injection: core_app_factory.py.

sections.already: Already in your repos: takeod-site uses gsap, ScrollTrigger, lenis and @splinetool/viewer (Spline 3D on a canvas) in src/motion.js, src/spline.js and src/nav.js. I found no three or @react-three yet.
sections.scene: Scene, camera, renderer: the three building blocks of every 3D page.
sections.camera: Perspective vs orthographic camera: realistic depth vs flat or isometric looks.
sections.mesh: Mesh = geometry + material: the shape plus how it looks.
sections.pbr: PBR materials (metalness/roughness): realistic gold and silver, relevant to your jewelry sites.
sections.textures: Textures and UVs: how images wrap onto models.
sections.lighting: Lighting (ambient, directional, point, spot, environment/HDRI): mood and realism.
sections.shadows: Shadows (shadow maps): realism, but expensive on mobile.
sections.webgl: WebGL: the browser GPU API under everything. WebGPU is its faster successor.
sections.three: Three.js: the standard JS 3D library and the step up from Spline when you need control.
sections.r3f: React Three Fiber (R3F): Three.js written as React components, which fits your React stack.
sections.drei: drei: ready-made R3F helpers (OrbitControls, useGLTF, Environment).
sections.useFrame: useFrame: an R3F hook for per-frame animation.
sections.gsap: GSAP timelines and ScrollTrigger: scroll-driven 3D storytelling, which you already use.
sections.lenis: Lenis smooth scroll: sync it with ScrollTrigger and the render loop to avoid jitter.
sections.perf: Performance basics: draw calls, polycount, texture size and compression (KTX2/Basis), instancing, LOD. These keep mobile and iPad smooth.
sections.dpr: devicePixelRatio cap (e.g. max 2) and frameloop="demand": big battery and FPS wins.
sections.dispose: Disposing geometries, materials and textures: prevents memory leaks in SPAs.
sections.compression: Draco / Meshopt compression: much smaller model downloads.
sections.glsl: GLSL shaders: vertex vs fragment shaders, uniforms, varyings and attributes, used for custom effects.
sections.gltf: glTF/GLB: the "JPEG of 3D" and best for the web. OBJ and FBX are older interchange formats.
sections.gltfjsx: gltfjsx: turns a GLB into an R3F component.

sections.linux: Linux shell, permissions, users, systemd services: keep Sam ERP running on sam-erp-cloud-1.
sections.ssh: SSH and keys: secure server access.
sections.uvicorn: Uvicorn, reverse proxy (Nginx/Caddy), HTTPS/TLS: production serving.
sections.digitalocean: DigitalOcean droplets, firewalls, backups/snapshots: your hosting.
sections.gcp: Google Cloud VM: the MGE scraper host.
sections.dns: DNS: domains, plus the fakedns issue you hit in tests.
sections.cicd: CI/CD: auto-test and deploy on merge.
sections.logs: Logs and monitoring: spot failures early (Always-Running).
sections.tailscale: Tailscale: private access without opening ports.

sections.erp: ERP, CRM, modules: what Sam ERP is.
sections.books: Chart of accounts, double-entry, P&L, reconciliation, categorization: Bookkeeper and the P&L work.
sections.irs: IRS forms (1040, Schedule C, 1099, W-2), draft return, e-file: Tax Expert work under Policies 02/03, where drafts are never filed.
sections.claims: Claims and collections, debts, credit: Financial Hub and Claims Hunter.
sections.pii: PII, data retention, client confidentiality: legal duty for tax data.
sections.dueDates: Due-date reminders and extensions: a core tax-season workflow.
